Calculus utilities

Source: R/zz-aliases.R
calculus-utils.Rd

singularities(f, x, domain) returns the points of domain where f is undefined (zeros of denominators and of logarithm arguments); the default domain is Reals for a real x and Complexes otherwise. stationary_points() solves f'(x) = 0 on a domain; minimum() and maximum() return the extreme values on a closed interval or the real line, including one-sided limits at poles. is_increasing(), is_strictly_increasing(), is_decreasing(), is_strictly_decreasing(), is_monotonic() and is_convex() test the sign of derivatives on an interval. periodicity(f, x) returns the period of trigonometric expressions. euler_equations(L, funcs, vars) gives the list of Euler-Lagrange equations of a Lagrangian, for derivatives of any order. finite_diff_weights(order, x_list, x0) returns Fornberg weights w[[m + 1]][[k]][[j]]: derivative order m, first k grid points, point j. apply_finite_diff() applies the full-grid weights.

Usage

singularities(f, x, domain = NULL)

stationary_points(f, x, domain = Reals)

minimum(f, x, domain = Reals)

maximum(f, x, domain = Reals)

is_increasing(f, interval = Reals, x = NULL)

is_strictly_increasing(f, interval = Reals, x = NULL)

is_decreasing(f, interval = Reals, x = NULL)

is_strictly_decreasing(f, interval = Reals, x = NULL)

is_monotonic(f, interval = Reals, x = NULL)

is_convex(f, x = NULL, domain = Reals)

periodicity(f, x)

euler_equations(L, funcs = NULL, vars = NULL)

finite_diff_weights(order, x_list, x0 = 1)

apply_finite_diff(order, x_list, y_list, x0 = 0)

Arguments

f, L

Expressions.

x

The variable.

domain

An interval, Reals or Complexes; for singularities(), NULL picks from the assumptions on x.

interval

An interval, or Reals.

funcs

Function applications such as u(x), a list of them, or NULL for all undefined functions in L.

vars

Independent variables, or NULL for the arguments of the first function.

order

Derivative order.

x_list, y_list

Grid points and values.

x0

Evaluation point.

Value

A set, expression, logical or list.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x")
singularities(1 / (x^2 - 1), x)
#> {-1, 1}
minimum(x^2 - 2*x, x)
#> -1
is_increasing(exp(x), Reals, x)
#> [1] TRUE
finite_diff_weights(1, list(-1, 0, 1), 0)[[2]][[3]]
#> [[1]]
#> -1/2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 0
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> 1/2
#>
